main_issue: Whether alcohol can be served at the housewarming in the flat, resolved by keeping the drinks in a cooler box outside the front door

A-B.evidence: B said 'looks good to me' (turn 2) about A's drinks; both endorsed the cooler outside the door (turns 17, 19). They never addressed each other directly.

A-C.evidence: C proposed the cooler outside the door and asked A (turn 15); A replied 'a cooler outside works for me' (turn 17).

A-D.evidence: A asked D if it was okay (turn 3) and D objected (turn 4). Later D agreed to the cooler outside (turn 14), A accepted it (turn 17), and A said 'that's settled' (turn 21).

B-C.evidence: C asked B whether the cooler works for the manager (turn 18); B said 'that works for me, thanks for sorting it out' (turn 19).

B-D.evidence: B wanted drinks for the manager (turn 10) while D refused alcohol at home (turns 4, 9). Both ended up agreeing to the cooler outside (turns 14, 19), and D said 'glad we worked it out' (turn 20).

C-D.evidence: C's kitchen idea was declined (turn 12), but D accepted C's cooler outside the door: 'I can agree to that. Thanks, Agent C' (turn 14).
